podcast.body: By 1978, when Kraftwerk released "The Model" (from The Man-Machine album), the band had been experimenting with synthesizer technology for approximately five years, leading to best-selling albums and hit songs on international charts. Their distinctive sound, characterized by a robotic, cold, artificial, emotionally sterile, and intense vibe, fascinated artists like David Bowie and significantly influenced the emergence of Technopop. "At the time, craft work released the model in 1978. They'd been experimenting with synthesizer technology for about five years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Considered by many electronic music scholars as the first "Techno" album in its modern sense, "Man-Machine" demonstrates a radical shift in Kraftwerk's style, moving from melody-focused synthesizer work to complex sampling and sequencing, with modern techno still resembling it significantly. "Para muchos estudiosos de la electrónica de man-machine grabbar es el primer álbum de música tecnotálico como lo conocemos."

podcast.body: Released in 1978, this album, alongside "Trans-Europe Express," defined Kraftwerk's electronic pop sound and achieved global success. It featured dance-pop hits like "Showroom Dummies" and "The Model," marking a breakthrough in creating universally appealing and danceable electronic music. "funcionó nindos del Dance Pop como Translíope Express, showroom dumis, de model, de robots, Crafwerke había logrado lo que muchas artistas llevaban años señando."
